2027-04-28.title: Wednesday of the fourth week after Qyomtho · Memory of Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon
readings: Remember your leaders; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever
2027-04-28.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection), the week after the Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho. The Panchangam keeps the memory of Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon (1987) and gives John 10:11–18, John 14:1–6 or John 15:9–17 as alternative Gospels.
2027-04-28.verse: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
theo: Today the Panchangam asks us to remember Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon, a bishop of our Church, who entered his rest in 1987. Forty years have passed, and many younger members of our Church will not know his face. The Letter to the Hebrews tells us why such remembering matters: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” The Church is not a club that begins again with each generation. It is a family with a memory. We received the faith from people who were baptized, taught, ordained and consecrated before us; they carried it through difficult years and handed it on. To remember them is to give thanks for them, to learn from them, and to pray for them. The Catholic Church has always prayed for her departed shepherds, asking that any stain of human weakness be washed away and that they may see the face of the Chief Shepherd. Then comes the line that holds all generations together: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.” Bishops come and go; the Lord they served does not change. The Christ who called Mar Yoohanon is the Christ who calls us.

Hebrews goes on to the heart of the bishop's service and of the whole Church's life: “We have an altar from which those who officiate in the tent have no right to eat.” Christians are not people without a sacrifice. Our altar is the altar of the Holy Qurbono, where the one sacrifice of Christ on Calvary is made present and his true Body and Blood are given as food. Hebrews explains with an image from the old temple: the bodies of the sacrificed animals were burned outside the camp, and “Therefore Jesus also suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood. Let us then go to him outside the camp and bear the abuse he endured. For here we have no lasting city, but we are looking for the city that is to come.” Two more sacrifices flow from the altar into daily life: “let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name,” and “Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.” Worship, praise and sharing belong together. St Augustine once told his people: for you I am a bishop, with you I am a Christian; the first is a burden, the second a grace (Sermon 340, in substance).

The Gospel gives the measure of every shepherd and every steward. “Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives.” A bishop gives the household its food: the word of God, the sacraments, wise guidance. But every Christian is a steward of something: parents of their children, teachers of their pupils, employers of their workers, the healthy of the sick who depend on them. The warning is sharp: the wicked servant who says “My master is delayed” and begins to beat his fellow servants and to drink with drunkards will be surprised by the master's return. Our Lord rose and ascended and will come again; we do not know the hour. Today, pray for the soul of Mar Yoohanon and for all the bishops and priests who served our Church and have gone before us. Pray for our present bishops. And ask yourself: in the household entrusted to me, am I giving food at the proper time?

The Church as a family with a memory; praying for our departed shepherds.
The sacrifice of Christ, the sacrifice of praise and the sacrifice of sharing.

live: Pray today for the soul of Mar Yoohanon and of one priest or catechist who taught you the faith and has died.
Think of one person who depends on you, and give them this week what they truly need: time, attention, a meal, a word of encouragement.
2027-04-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Chief Shepherd of the flock, you are the same yesterday and today and forever. We remember before you your servant Isaac Mar Yoohanon, who spoke your word to your people and served at your altar. Forgive him every human weakness, and bring him to the city that is to come, to rejoice in the light of your face. Give your Church faithful and wise shepherds, who feed your household at the proper time. Make each of us a faithful steward of what you have entrusted to us, ready to be found at work when you come. Let us offer you a continual sacrifice of praise and never neglect to do good and to share. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: We have an altar: in the Holy Qurbono the one sacrifice of Christ, who suffered outside the gate to sanctify us by his own blood, is made present, and the faithful servants of every age are fed with his Body and Blood.

quick: Hebrews: remember your leaders who spoke God's word to you, and imitate their faith; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
We have an altar: the sacrifice of Christ, from which flow the sacrifice of praise and the sacrifice of doing good and sharing.
The faithful and wise servant gives the household its food at the proper time and is found at work when the master comes.
2027-04-28.action: Pray for a priest, bishop or catechist who taught you the faith and has died.
2027-04-28.question: In the household God has entrusted to me, am I giving food at the proper time?

family.explain: Today our Church remembers a bishop, Isaac Mar Yoohanon, who died forty years ago. The Bible tells us to remember the people who taught us about God and to copy their faith. Jesus also tells a story about a good servant whose master put him in charge of feeding the whole house. The servant did his job faithfully, and the master was very happy. Each of us has a job from God: helping at home, doing homework, being kind to brothers and sisters.
family.intention: We pray for the bishops and priests who have died, and for our bishops and priests today.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught each of us about Jesus? Let us thank God for them by name.”

illus: An imagined story, about another bishop whose name is not given. In a parish near Thiruvalla the old sacristy cupboard held a worn black leather case with a chalice inside. One day a young altar server asked why it was kept there when the parish had newer chalices. The vicar told him that a bishop had used it when he came to the village on foot during the monsoon, many decades ago, to celebrate the Qurbono in a church with a thatched roof. The bishop had baptized the vicar's own grandfather. On the bishop's memorial day the vicar used that chalice. The boy served at that Qurbono, and afterwards he said he had felt as if the whole line of them were standing behind him: the bishop, the grandfather, the priests in between.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are the same yesterday and today and forever. We thank you for the shepherds who gave us the faith. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders... and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Whose faith do I want to imitate?
Let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God (Hebrews 13:15). Is praise a daily part of my life?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What work has the Lord entrusted to me?
pm.resp: Lord, give rest to your servants and strength to your Church.
interc: For the soul of Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon and all the departed bishops, priests and religious of our Church.
For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and priests, that they may be faithful and wise stewards.
For parents, teachers and all who are responsible for others, that they may give food at the proper time.
For those who have no lasting city: refugees, migrants and the homeless.
For our parish, that our worship at the altar may become praise on our lips and generosity in our hands.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the same yesterday and today and forever. Grant eternal rest to the shepherds who served your people, give your Church faithful stewards in every age, and make us ready to be found at work when he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today our Church remembers Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon, a bishop who entered his rest in 1987. Hebrews tells us: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:7–8).

Hebrews also says: we have an altar (Hebrews 13:10). Jesus suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood (Hebrews 13:12), and that sacrifice is made present at every Holy Qurbono. From the altar flow two more sacrifices: praise on our lips, and doing good and sharing what we have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God (Hebrews 13:15–16).

In the Gospel Jesus asks: who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? (Matthew 24:45). That is the work of a bishop and a priest, but each of us is a steward too: of children, of workers, of the sick, of the poor at our gate.

Let us pray today for the soul of Mar Yoohanon and all our departed shepherds, and for our bishops now. And let us be found at work when the Lord comes: faithful at the altar, generous with our neighbours, giving food at the proper time to those who depend on us. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today we remember a bishop called Isaac Mar Yoohanon, who went home to God forty years ago. Bishops are like shepherds who take care of God's family. Jesus told a story about a servant who was put in charge of giving food to everyone in the house, and he did it well every day. God gives you jobs too: helping Amma, sharing with your little brother or sister, saying your prayers. If you do them well, Jesus will be very happy when he sees you!

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
On the memory of Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon: remembering our shepherds, the altar we have, and the faithful steward.

sub: Considering the outcome of their life.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
And when the chief shepherd appears, you will win the crown of glory that never fades away.
points.apply: Pray today by name for the departed bishops and priests who served your parish or family.

sub: Outside the camp, looking for the city to come.
The sacrifices of praise and of sharing.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering
The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a sharing in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a sharing in the body of Christ?
points.apply: Make one act of sharing this week, in money, time or food, as an offering flowing from the altar.

sub: Found at work when he comes.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Think of us in this way, as servants of Christ and stewards of God’s mysteries. Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
points.apply: Name one person who depends on you and give them what they truly need this week.

concl: Shepherds pass; the Christ they served is the same yesterday and today and forever.
Every Christian is a steward, and the Lord will come to find us at work.
2027-04-28.resolve: Remember and pray for those who gave you the faith, live from the altar, and be a faithful steward of what God has entrusted to you.
